summary: Stephen Batchelor works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Songgwangsa, Tibet Institute Rikon, and the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives under Richard Gombrich, Kusan Sunim, and others. He led Sharpham College (~1992–2000) and joined Bodhi College (~2015).

Stephen C. Berkwitz works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya (1995–1997) and held posts at Missouri State University, where he was Associate Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2004), and Ruhr University Bochum.

Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University under Alan Sponberg and Denis Twitchett, later teaching at Middlebury College and Princeton, where he became a professor in 2005.

Stephen Fuchs worked in Indology and religious studies, earning his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna under Wilhelm Schmidt. He founded the Anthropos Institute and Institute of Indian Culture, and taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1950–1954) and University of San Carlos.

Stephen G. Covell is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies at Princeton University under Jacqueline I. Stone (~1995–2001) and held a post at Western Michigan University (~2003).

Stephen H. Phillips is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He served as a professor of philosophy (attested 1999) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026) at the University of Texas at Austin.

Stephen Harris specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of New Mexico in 2014 and serves as a University Lecturer in Indian and Comparative Philosophy at Leiden University (attested 2026).

Stephen J. Laumakis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, George J. Tanabe, and David West, and served as Associate Professor in the Philosophy Department at the University of St. Thomas (attested 2008–2013).

Stephen Jenkins specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University under doctoral supervisors Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey, among other teachers. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (attested 2010–2013).

Stephen Prothero is a religious studies scholar. He studied at Yale and Harvard University, completing his Ph.D. under William R. Hutchison (1986–1990). In ~1996 he joined Boston University, becoming Professor Emeritus of Religion in America.

Stephen R. Bokenkamp specializes in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley (~1974–1986) and held posts at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2007) and Arizona State University (~2007), along with a visiting fellowship at Australian National University (1999).
Stephen Suen is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2009).

Stephen Wootton Bushell was a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Guy's Hospital Medical School and the University of London, and held medical posts at Guy's Hospital (1866) and Bethlem Royal Hospital (1867).

Steve Odin is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Stony Brook University under David A. Dilworth and Edward S. Casey, and became a Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʱi at Mānoa in 1982.

Steven Collins was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich, held posts at Bristol and Indiana University, and became Chester D. Tripp Professor in the Humanities at the University of Chicago (1991).

Steven Edward Lindquist works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin in 2005 under Patrick Olivelle, alongside several traditional teachers, and held a post at Concordia University.

Steven Heine is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Temple University, and held academic posts at Villanova, La Salle, Pennsylvania State University (~1989–1997), and Florida International University (1997).

Steven Lukes works in philosophy. He studied at Oxford under Edward Evan Evans-Pritchard and held posts at Balliol College (1966–1987), European University Institute, University of Florence, University of Siena, London School of Economics (~2001–2006), and New York University (~2006–2021).

Steven Neal Weinberger specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins in 2003, and was affiliated with the University of Virginia (attested 2006).
Stewart McFarlane works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held posts in the Department of Religious Studies at Lancaster University (attested 1991 and 2001).
